*   [![Image 8: 【机器人生态圈】②韩国五年后"一无所有"？ 人形机器人产业站上十字路口](https://image.ajunews.com/content/image/2025/09/17/20250917164031324088.jpg) 【机器人生态圈】②韩国五年后"一无所有"？ 人形机器人产业站上十字路口 “按照目前的趋势发展下去，五年后会一无所有。”韩国科学技术研究院（KIST）AI机器人研究所人形机器人研究团李伊洙博士，直言不讳表达出对本国人形机器人产业的忧虑。当美国凭借人工智能与资本领先全球，中国依靠平台和大量生产迅速追赶时，韩国依旧在“能否赚钱”的疑问前踟蹰不前。韩国几乎没有成型的部件与软件生态，一旦未能建立自主产业体系，最终可能必须依附于海外供应链。 ◆上游依赖加深 产业生态“空心” 韩国机器人零部件对外依存度极高。业内人士直言，国内企业根本不接小额订单，想要研发必须买中国的零部件，或者自己慢慢做。问题的核心在于需求不足。韩国机器人产业协会下属零部件委员会会长柳在完指出：“目前零部件销售几乎没有收入。至少要到2030年以后，人形机器人才能真正进入产线。” 数据显示，韩国核心零部件减速器国产化率为35.8%，电机38.8%，传感器42.5%，控制器47.9%，整体偏低。其中减速器70%依赖日本，伺服电机和控制器也大部分来自中日。相反，中国的产业化速度令人瞩目，工业机器人国产化率从2018年的27.3%升至2023年的47.2%，伺服驱动器国产化率更是高达90%。 这一差距的背后是截然不同的政策力度。中国政府设立1万亿人民币规模的基金，而韩国K-人形机器人联盟的政府支持资金不足1万亿韩元。如果关键零部件持续依赖中国，韩国不仅会失去自主能力，还可能沦为中国机器人产业链的一环。高度依赖制造业的韩国对这种风险尤其敏感。人形机器人是有望取代工厂一线人力的“潜在主角”，一旦核心技术缺位，制造业则根基难保。 K-人形机器人联盟总会【图片来源 韩国产业通商资源部】 ◆大厂起步太晚 CES或成转折？ 面对这一现状，韩国大型企业正在加速布局。三星、LG、现代汽车计划在2026年1月的国际消费类电子产品展览会（CES）上首次公开人形机器人产品。业内普遍认为，韩国企业必须借此机会在全球舞台展示实力。 三星目前已经成立未来机器人推进团，与子公司Rainbow Robotics协作研发；LG由机器人先行研究所和家电部门联合推动，专注家庭场景；现代汽车则依托研发本部与旗下波士顿动力分工合作，强化硬件与软件。不过，除了波士顿动力的Atlas以外，韩国企业尚无成熟商用产品。 与此同时，AeiRobot、Robotis、Robros等多家本土中小企业也计划在今年下半年推出人形机器人。政府主导的K-人形机器人联盟计划在CES设立专馆，集中展示研发成果。这会是韩国人形机器人产业的一次关键亮相，但能否借机实现突破，还取决于后续投资与生态建设。 波士顿动力研发的人形机器人Atlas【图片来源 波士顿动力】 ◆困于“信赖资本” 投资政策保守 相比中美，韩国机器人产业更大的问题在于思维模式。“韩国大型企业和政府总问能不能赚钱，所以迟迟不敢推动。”李伊洙博士指出。中美两国的企业会先行测试，再逐步改进，而韩国则一开始就纠结于成本、安全与短期收益。另一位专家则直言，韩国大型企业似乎也仅仅是看“气氛”在做机器人。 韩国政府的支持政策也偏于谨慎。Robros公司首席技术官（CTO）朴贤俊透露：“政府项目通常都是三四年周期，而AI和机器人产业发展远远快于这个节奏。”此外，公共机构采购时甚至只愿意买与项目周期对应的许可证，缺乏长期视角。 资本市场同样保守。中国和美国机器人产业的飞跃离不开大规模风投资金与企业投入。在韩国，投资行业更加看重短期回报。一位风投企业代表坦言，低迷的市场环境下大家都不愿冒险，韩国企业的反应确实比国际竞争对手慢了一步。 ◆“未来汽车产业” 韩国还在犹豫 在严峻的现实情况下，韩国也并非没有期待。首尔大学教授朴在兴认为，人形机器人有望像汽车和电脑一样，成为未来全球的支柱产业。市场调研机构Strategy Analytics预测，截至2035年，全球人形机器人市场规模或达1万亿美元，与当前全球汽车市场规模相当。 也就是说，人形机器人不再只是科技噱头，而是未来工业制造、家庭服务乃至整个社会结构的潜在关键。韩国机器人产业目前正处在继续犹豫“能否赚钱”和决心建立自主生态的十字路口，而在全球资本与技术加速汇聚的当下，留给韩国的时间可能并不多。 2025-09-17 16:45:17](https://www.ajudaily.com/view/20250917080250136)

11.title: Global Robot Demand in Factories Doubles Over 10 Years
11.description: The new World Robotics 2025 statistics on industrial robots showed 542,000 robots installed in 2024 - more than double the number 10 years ago. Annual installations topped 500,000 units for the fourth straight year. Asia accounted for 74% of new deployments in 2024, compared with 16% in Europe and 9% in the Americas.
11.content:
### World Robotics 2025 Report by International Federation of Robotics released

_Frankfurt, Sep 25, 2025 —_ The new World Robotics 2025 statistics on industrial robots showed 542,000 robots installed in 2024 - more than double the number 10 years ago. Annual installations topped 500,000 units for the fourth straight year. Asia accounted for 74% of new deployments in 2024, compared with 16% in Europe and 9% in the Americas.

![Image 1: A bar graph shows the annual installations of industrial robots worldwide in thousands of units from 2014 to 2024](https://ifr.org/downloads/press_docs/Teaser_global_market_2014_-_2024.jpg)

“The new World Robotics statistics show 2024 the second highest annual installation count of industrial robots in history - only 2% lower than the all-time-high two years ago,” says Takayuki Ito, President of the International Federation of Robotics. “The transition of many industries into the digital and automated age has been marked by a huge surge in demand. The total number of industrial robots in operational use worldwide was 4,664,000 units in 2024 – an increase of 9% compared to the previous year.”

Asia, Europe and the Americas - overview
----------------------------------------

**China**is by far the world’s largest market in 2024, representing 54% of global deployments. The latest figures show that 295,000 industrial robots have been installed - the highest annual total on record. For the first time, Chinese manufacturers have sold more than foreign suppliers in their home country. Their domestic market share climbed to 57% last year, up from about 28% over the past decade. China’s operational robot stock exceeded the 2 million mark in 2024, the largest of any country. As robotics in China is opening up new markets, there is no indication that robot demand in China will decrease. There is still a lot of potential in Chinese manufacturing for 10% growth on average each year until 2028.

**Japan**maintained its position as the second-largest market for industrial robots, with 44,500 units installed in 2024 – a slight 4% decrease. The country's operational stock rose by 3%, with 450,500 units now in use. Demand for robots will grow slightly by lower single-digit rates in 2025. It will then accelerate to a medium single-digit rate on average in the next few years.

The market in the **Republic of Korea** installed 30,600 units in 2024 – down 3%. Annual installations had been trending sideways of around 31,000 units since 2019. The country is the fourth largest robot market in the world in terms of annual installations in 2024, after the United States, Japan, and China.

**India**continues to grow with a record of 9,100 units installed in 2024 – up 7%. The automotive industry was the strongest driver with a market share of 45%. In terms of annual installations, India ranks sixth worldwide, one place up behind Germany.

Europe
------

Industrial robot installations in **Europe**fell 8% to 85,000 units in 2024, still the second largest number recorded in history. 80% of all European robot installations took place in the European Union (67,800 units). Robot demand in Europe benefited from the nearshoring trend. The annual average growth rate from 2019 to 2024 was plus 3%.

**Germany**is the largest robot market in Europe and the fifth-largest in the world. Installations fell 5% to 26,982 units in 2024, which is the second-best result recorded after the record year of 2023. This represents a 32% market share of the annual total in Europe. The number of installations in **Italy**, the second largest European market, fell by 16% to 8,783 units. **Spain**is now in third place (5,100 units), with a strong demand from the automotive industry. **France**(4,900 units) moved down to fourth place, with a 24% decrease.

In the **UK**, industrial robot installations were down 35% to 2,500 units in 2024. The record number of 3,800 units in 2023 was a one-off peak, driven by the “super-deduction” tax credit program, which ended after the first quarter of 2023. Installation counts moved sideways with some cyclicity over the past decade. Robot installations in the UK rank 19th worldwide in 2024.

The Americas
------------

Robot installations in the Americas exceeded 50,000 units for the fourth year in a row: 50,100 units were installed in 2024, down 10% below the level reached 2023.

The **United States**, the largest regional market, accounted for 68% of installations in the Americas in 2024. Robot installations were down by 9% to 34,200 units. The United States imports most of its robots from Japan and Europe, with few domestic suppliers. However, there are numerous domestic robot system integrators implementing robotic automation solutions.

Total installations in **Mexico**reached 5,600 units in 2024, a decrease of 4%. The automotive industry remained the key customer of industrial robots in Mexico, accounting for 63% of the installations in 2024.

In **Canada**, robot installations declined by 12% to 3,800 units. Installation figures in Canada largely depend on automotive investment cycles. The share of the car industry was 47% in 2024.

Outlook
-------

The OECD and the IMF expect global growth in a range of 2.9% to 3.0% in 2025 and 2.9% and 3.1% in 2026. However, geopolitical tensions, violent conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, and trade disruptions are exerting their negative impact on the global economy.

The robotics industry is not immune to global macroeconomic conditions, but there is no indication that the overall long-term growth trend will come to an end any time soon. While regional trends vary substantially, the aggregate global trajectory remains positive. Globally, robot installations are expected to grow by 6% to 575,000 units in 2025. By 2028, the 700,000-unit mark will be surpassed.

Global robot demand in factories doubles over a decade
======================================================

Evertiq

Global demand for industrial robots has more than doubled in the past ten years, according to the International Federation of Robotics (IFR). The latest World Robotics 2025 report shows that 542,000 new robots were installed in factories during 2024, marking the fourth consecutive year with installations above 500,000 units.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Asia accounted for the majority of deployments, representing 74% of new installations, compared with 16% in Europe and 9% in the Americas.

> “The new World Robotics statistics show 2024 was the second-highest annual installation count of industrial robots in history - only 2% lower than the all-time high two years ago,” said IFR President Takayuki Ito. “The transition of many industries into the digital and automated age has been marked by a huge surge in demand. The total number of industrial robots in operational use worldwide was 4,664,000 units in 2024 – an increase of 9% compared to the previous year.”

**Asia leads the global market**

China remained the largest market, with 295,000 installations in 2024, representing 54% of the global deployments. For the first time, domestic manufacturers sold more units than foreign suppliers in China, reaching a 57% market share. The country’s operational stock exceeded two million robots. IFR projects annual growth of around 10% in the Chinese market through 2028.

Japan, the second-largest market, saw 44,500 installations in 2024, a 4% decline from the previous year. The Republic of Korea ranked fourth worldwide with 30,600 units, down 3%. India continued its upward trajectory with a record 9,100 installations, up 7% year-on-year, led by demand from the automotive sector.

**Europe records decline**

In Europe, industrial robot installations fell 8% to 85,000 units, though this was still the second-highest figure on record. Germany accounted for nearly a third of the European total with 26,982 installations, down 5% from 2023. Italy recorded 8,783 units, a 16% decrease, while Spain and France followed with 5,100 and 4,900 units, respectively. In the UK, installations dropped 35% to 2,500 units, reflecting the end of the temporary “super-deduction” tax incentive in 2023.

**Americas weaken**

Installations in the Americas totalled 50,100 units in 2024, a 10% decline. The United States led with 34,200 installations, down 9% from the previous year. Mexico and Canada followed with 5,600 and 3,800 units, respectively, both registering declines linked largely to fluctuations in automotive investment.

**Outlook remains positive**

Despite weaker results in several regions, IFR forecasts a resumption of growth in 2025. Global robot installations are expected to rise 6% to 575,000 units in 2025, surpassing 700,000 by 2028. While geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty remain risks, IFR said long-term demand for automation in manufacturing remains strong.

China leads global industrial robot market with record installations: IFR-Xinhua
===============

China leads global industrial robot market with record installations: IFR
=========================================================================

Source: Xinhua

Editor: huaxia

2025-09-25 22:14:00

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=http://www.chinaview.cn/20250925/6fd79028f7f541daafe98129ee692ae9/c.html "分享到Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=China%20leads%20global%20industrial%20robot%20market%20with%20record%20installations:%20IFR&url=http://www.chinaview.cn/20250925/6fd79028f7f541daafe98129ee692ae9/c.html "分享到Twitter")[![Image 6: A complex QR code in black and white](http://www.chinaview.cn/20250925/6fd79028f7f541daafe98129ee692ae9/zxcode_202509256fd79028f7f541daafe98129ee692ae9.jpg)](http://www.chinaview.cn/20250925/6fd79028f7f541daafe98129ee692ae9/c.html "分享到微信")[](https://service.weibo.com/share/share.php?title=China%20leads%20global%20industrial%20robot%20market%20with%20record%20installations:%20IFR&url=http://www.chinaview.cn/20250925/6fd79028f7f541daafe98129ee692ae9/c.html "分享到新浪微博")

BERLIN, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- China's industrial robot stock reached a record 2,027,000 units in 2024, accounting for more than half of global demand, according to the World Robotics 2025 report released Thursday by the Frankfurt-based International Federation of Robotics (IFR).

Annual installations in China climbed to 295,000 units, up 7 percent from 2023, marking the highest level ever recorded, the report said. Globally, 542,000 industrial robots were installed in 2024, more than double the number a decade ago, and worldwide installations exceeded 500,000 units for the fourth consecutive year.

"China's strategy to modernize its manufacturing base has reached a new milestone in the country's automation push," IFR President Takayuki Ito said. "The robot stock doubled within three years, surpassing 1 million units in 2021 and now counting 2 million units in 2024."

Asia remained the dominant market, accounting for 74 percent of new robot deployments in 2024, compared with 16 percent in Europe and 9 percent in the Americas.

In China, the electrical and electronics sector continued to lead demand with 83,000 units installed in 2024, followed by the automotive industry with 57,200 units. Domestic suppliers also expanded their presence in food processing, textiles and wood products.

For the first time, Chinese robot makers sold more units at home than foreign competitors, with their domestic market share rising to 57 percent in 2024 from 47 percent in 2023, the report noted. IFR's Q1 2025 survey also showed strong double-digit growth in robot orders across Asia, largely driven by China.

Worldwide, the total number of industrial robots in operation reached 4,664,000 units in 2024, a 9 percent increase from the previous year. Ito said that while global macroeconomic conditions may create short-term headwinds, the long-term growth trend remains strong.

The report forecasts that the global robotics industry will maintain robust growth. Worldwide installations are expected to rise 6 percent to 575,000 units in 2025 and to surpass 700,000 units by 2028, with average annual growth around 10 percent until then. China is expected to remain the world's largest market beyond that period. ■

中国工业机器人第一大省：去年生产16.88万台，超过上海+江苏之和
=================================

2024-12-06 19:28·[新潮商评论](http://m.toutiao.com/c/user/token/MS4wLjABAAAA2mlpnRlfI9bAFwWWgyYxuj5ZDe9VbVHrChPbqLanb4o/?source=tuwen_detail)

作品声明：内容取材于网络

根据国际机器人联合会（IFR）发布《2024世界机器人报告》显示，全球有约428万台机器人在工厂运行，同比增长10%。机器人密度（每万名制造业工人安装的机器人数量）上升至162台/万人，创下历史新高，是七年前（2016年74台/万人）的两倍多。欧盟、北美、亚洲的机器人密度分别为219台/万人（+5.2%）、197台/万人（+4.2%）、182台/万人（+7.6%）。

![Image 6: Robot density in the manufacturing industry in 2023, where Republic of Korea and Singapore have the highest density of robots, and world density is 162 robots installed per 10,000 employees](https://p3-sign.toutiaoimg.com/tos-cn-i-axegupay5k/e9a6225b54164c0c8f5c552700628cde~tplv-tt-origin-web:gif.jpeg?_iz=58558&from=article.pc_detail&lk3s=953192f4&x-expires=1766939945&x-signature=pX2QgWbc3lzqlwpu1HPojz9tjE4%3D)

这个数字也是观察各个国家/地区制造业自动化的重要指标。**韩国**位居世界第一，每一万名员工配有1,012台机器人；自2018年以来，在电子工业和汽车行业的推动下，机器人密度平均每年增加5%。紧随其后的是**新加坡**（770台/万人），其中，电子行业占75%至90%的份额。

**中国**以470台/万人的机器人密度上升到第三，排名四至十位的分别是德国（429台/万人）、日本（419台/万人）、瑞典（347台/万人）、中国香港（322台/万人）、丹麦（306台/万人）、斯洛文尼亚（306台/万人）、瑞士（302台/万人）。

![Image 7: Several bright yellow robot arms extend over a conveyor belt line](https://p3-sign.toutiaoimg.com/tos-cn-i-6w9my0ksvp/612c00b9bb0f4fb2aa2566efcd23c357~tplv-tt-origin-web:gif.jpeg?_iz=58558&from=article.pc_detail&lk3s=953192f4&x-expires=1766939945&x-signature=tvIKEpyCEffXOPs8f1y5OOoseCU%3D)

2019年，中国机器人密度为206台/万人，首次跻身全球前十。短短四年时间，每万名工厂工人的机器人比例就增加了一倍多。要知道我国拥有约3700万制造业从业人员，单论工业机器人数量，我国已经连续11年成为全球最大工业机器人市场，保有量约180万台。

去年共安装276,288台工业机器人，占全球安装总量的51%，最近三年占比均过半。其次是日本（4.61万台）、美国（3.76万台）、韩国（3.14万台）、德国（2.84万台）。

![Image 8: Robotic welding machine in factory, creating sparks](https://p3-sign.toutiaoimg.com/tos-cn-i-6w9my0ksvp/2a7fb914e47b43848b7077a825e644b7~tplv-tt-origin-web:gif.jpeg?_iz=58558&from=article.pc_detail&lk3s=953192f4&x-expires=1766939945&x-signature=LhwjHjphlJNRDnoKg5OzeRAZN3s%3D)

据国家统计局数据显示，去年我国工业机器人产量达到42.95万台（套）。从省份来看，排名2-10位的分别是上海、江苏、浙江、天津、安徽、山东、辽宁、湖北、河北。

长三角地区是我国重要的工业机器人集聚区，三省一市均进入前十，占量占比超过四成。上海是全国首个把机器人密度纳入统计的城市，重点产业规上工业企业机器人密度达到426台/万人，处于世界领先水平，“四大家族”(发那科、A B B、安川和库卡)以及新时达、节卡、新松等本土企业，均在此有布局。

江苏、浙江、安徽拥有良好的制造业基础，为机器人研发奠定了良好基础。江苏的机器人产业园数量全国领先，形成了苏州、南京、常州为代表的机器人产业集聚城市。

值得一提的是，长三角地区也是我国重要的工业机器人出口基地。今年上半年，工业机器人出口同比增长16.8%，占全国份额高达49.5%。

![Image 9: Automated robot arm working on a production line, enclosed by a safety cage](https://p3-sign.toutiaoimg.com/tos-cn-i-6w9my0ksvp/beac21dff37e4fab8e1c9a04f0bdc4c5~tplv-tt-origin-web:gif.jpeg?_iz=58558&from=article.pc_detail&lk3s=953192f4&x-expires=1766939945&x-signature=X%2Fk4JRqW6dNvodXXv471wJz%2Boxw%3D)

**广东**连续4年位居全国第一，去年工业机器人产量达到16.88万台（套），全国每3台工业机器人就有一台是“广东造”。今年上半年，全省工业机器人产量同比增长37.6%，已经占到全国一半以上。【注：今年1-6月，我国工业机器人产量为28.3万台（套），同比增长9.6%】

从产业分布来看，主要集中在珠三角地区，广深佛莞四地均有相对完善的机器人产业集群，其中，广东、深圳集聚了大量高校与科研院所，分别坐拥省机器人创新中心和省具身智能机器人创新中心，可以提供技术支持和人才储备。

珠三角也是全球机器人第一大应用市场，拥有最多的应用场景。在自身制造业基础上，广州正加快推动以面向汽车、船舶、航空等高端制造业为主的集成应用；深圳推动以面向3C产业为主的工业机器人及集成应用；佛山聚焦工业机器人在家电、陶瓷、纺织等重点行业的集成应用；东莞则侧重于工业机器人在电子信息制造业、电气机械及设备制造业的集成应用。

根据规划，到2025年，广东省智能机器人产业营业收入将达800亿元，工业机器人年产量超过18万台（套）。组织实施500个以上智能制造示范项目，打造一批“机器人+”应用标杆企业。

The global [robot market](https://market.us/report/global-robot-market/) is on a remarkable growth path, with its value expected to soar from **USD 48.2 billion** in 2024 to an impressive **USD 233.7 billion** by 2034. This expansion represents a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 17.1%, propelled by rapid advances in automation technologies, artificial intelligence, and their increasing adoption across diverse industries worldwide. Notably, the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region dominates the market landscape, capturing over **62.2%** of the share with revenue reaching USD 29.98 billion in 2024. This stronghold is attributed to accelerated industrialization, governments’ proactive support for technological innovation, and investments in automation infrastructure.

Economic Benefits and Industry Transformation
---------------------------------------------

The surge in robotics adoption is profoundly impacting global economies by improving industrial productivity and reducing operational expenditures. Automated systems enhance efficiency, minimize human error, and accelerate manufacturing, leading to higher output quality and faster turnaround times. These benefits attract investments and innovation, fueling economic expansion and competitiveness on a global scale.

However, this transformation also brings workforce challenges. The displacement of traditional jobs due to automation creates an urgent need for reskilling and upskilling programs to prepare the labor force for collaboration with robotic technologies. Investments in education and training are essential to bridge the skills gap, mitigate disruption risks, and unlock new employment opportunities created by tech-driven industries. Consequently, robotics is emerging as a critical driver of sustainable economic growth and technological progress for countries embracing this shift.

Robotics Driving Change Across Multiple Industries
--------------------------------------------------

Global businesses are adapting strategically to capitalize on robotics’ potential amid evolving market dynamics. While the upfront capital requirements to implement robotic systems remain high, particularly for small and midsize enterprises, the long-term benefits such as operational cost reduction, enhanced precision, and scalability are considerable.

**Robotics is influencing key sectors as follows:**

*   Manufacturing: Automation facilitates increased production speed and precision, enabling manufacturers to meet growing demand efficiently while maintaining high-quality standards. Robotics also allows for flexible transfer between product lines, reducing downtime and waste.

*   Healthcare: The integration of robots in healthcare has transformed surgical procedures through precision-guided robotic arms, improved diagnostics with intelligent imaging systems, and enhanced patient care via automated monitoring devices, raising standards and reducing errors.

*   Logistics: Robotics is revolutionizing warehousing and delivery operations. Autonomous mobile robots streamline inventory management and last-mile delivery, improving speed, accuracy, and scalability in supply chains globally.

*   Agriculture: Precision farming robots optimize resource usage, monitor crop health, and automate labor-intensive tasks. This drives higher yields while promoting sustainable practices by reducing environmental impacts.

Strategic Business Approaches in a Robotics-Driven World
--------------------------------------------------------

To remain competitive and maximize the value derived from robotics, businesses are adopting informed strategies:

*   Workforce Empowerment: Prioritizing training and development to equip employees with skills necessary to operate alongside robotic systems fosters smooth integration and enhances productivity.

*   Collaborative Partnerships: Forming alliances with robotics technology providers and research institutions accelerates innovation cycles and allows for tailored solutions that meet specific operational needs.

*   Gradual Automation: Deploying robotics incrementally helps mitigate integration risks, allows time for process optimization, and facilitates cultural adaptation within organizations.

*   Regulatory and Ethical Compliance: Keeping abreast of evolving governmental policies and ethical guidelines ensures responsible use of robotic technology and builds stakeholder trust.

Regional Insights Highlight APAC’s Dominance
--------------------------------------------

The APAC region stands as the powerhouse of the global robot market, with a commanding 62.2% market share in 2024 fueled by aggressive industrial growth, government incentives, and expansive adoption of automation in manufacturing hubs such as China, Japan, and South Korea. North America and Europe sustain robust growth driven by their innovation ecosystems, technological advancements, and demand for more sophisticated robotic applications in service and specialized sectors like healthcare. Meanwhile, emerging markets in Latin America and the Middle East are witnessing rising interest in robotic solutions to combat rising labor costs and improve operational efficiencies, signaling new avenues for growth and investment.

Unlocking Opportunities in Robotics
-----------------------------------

The expanding robot market is ushering in a wealth of business opportunities across multiple dimensions. There is a surge in the development and deployment of specialized robots designed to meet niche needs—for example, surgical robots tailored to specific procedures or agricultural robots specialized to regional crop types. Additionally, the servicing, maintenance, and upgrade sectors for robotic systems are rapidly growing as businesses seek to maximize uptime and extend equipment life cycles.

Software enterprises focusing on AI and machine learning algorithms customized for robotic platforms offer immense potential, enhancing robot intelligence and adaptability. Notably, sustainability is reshaping opportunities, with green robotics and energy-efficient designs gaining traction amid global environmental concerns. The unfolding demand in emerging economies also presents fertile ground for innovative collaborations and market expansion.

Market Segmentation and Growth Drivers
--------------------------------------

The global robotics market segments itself primarily by type, application, and geography:

*   Types: Industrial robots currently dominate given their vast utility in manufacturing. Service robots and collaborative robots (cobots), which work alongside humans, are rapidly gaining traction thanks to their flexibility and expanding applications.

*   Applications: Robotics spans manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, agriculture, and retail. Automation demand, precision needs, labor cost pressures, and regulatory support are key growth factors influencing these segments.

*   Geography: APAC leads the market substantially due to accelerated industrialization. North America and Europe follow as mature markets driven by continuous innovation. Latin America and Middle East & Africa are emerging as new growth frontiers.

-----------------------------------------

Top market players concentrate on integrating AI to enhance robot autonomy, flexibility, and decision-making capabilities. Diversifying product portfolios to serve varied sectors and customizing solutions to client-specific environments remain priorities. Analyst Perspective: A Robust Future Outlook
--------------------------------------------

Market analysts project an optimistic trajectory for the robot sector driven by ceaseless advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning, which broaden robotic capabilities and foster novel applications. Adoption beyond large enterprises to small and medium-sized enterprises is expected to diversify growth and democratize technology access. Although initial capital and workforce adaptation hurdles exist today, these challenges are anticipated to lessen as technology matures and integration best practices evolve. As a key enabler of Industry 4.0, robotics will underpin future resilient manufacturing ecosystems and sustainable economic transformation globally.

About the Global Robot Market Growth
------------------------------------

The dynamic expansion of the global robot market embodies a fundamental shift toward smarter, more efficient, and technology-enabled industries worldwide. With continued investments in innovation and infrastructure, the market is positioned to redefine productivity thresholds and economic resilience over the next decade and beyond. 79.title: Global Robot Density in Factories Doubled in Seven Years
79.description: Robot adoption in factories around the world continues at high speed: The new global average robot density reaches a record 162 units per 10,000 employees in 2023 - more than double the number measured only seven years ago (74 units). This is according to the World Robotics 2024 report, presented by the International Federation of Robotics (IFR).
79.content:
### New World Robotics Data by International Federation of Robotics reveal

_Frankfurt, Nov 20, 2024 —_ Robot adoption in factories around the world continues at high speed: The new global average robot density reaches a record 162 units per 10,000 employees in 2023 - more than double the number measured only seven years ago (74 units). This is according to the World Robotics 2024 report, presented by the International Federation of Robotics (IFR).

![Image 1: Robot density in the manufacturing industry in 2023 represented in a blue bar chart, with Korea having 1,012 robots installed per 10,000 employees, followed by Singapore at 770, and China at 470](https://ifr.org/downloads/press2018/Teaser_Robot_Density_.jpg)

Robot density serves as a barometer to track the degree of automation adoption in the manufacturing industry around the world," says Takayuki Ito, President of the International Federation of Robotics. “This year's runner-up is China, which ranks third worldwide behind Korea and Singapore, but right up with Germany and Japan."

Robot density by region
-----------------------

The **European Union** has a robot density of 219 units per 10,000 employees, an increase of 5.2%, with Germany, Sweden, Denmark and Slovenia in the global top ten.

**North America´s** robot density is 197 units per 10,000 employees – up 4,2%. The United States ranks tenth in the world among the most automated countries in the manufacturing industry.

**Asia** has a robot density of 182 units per 10,000 persons employed in manufacturing - an increase of 7.6%. The economies of Korea, Singapore, mainland China and Japan are among the top ten most automated countries.

Top countries
-------------

The **Republic of Korea**is the world´s number one adopter of industrial robots with 1,012 robots per 10,000 employees. Robot density has increased by 5% on average each year since 2018. With a world-renowned electronics industry and a strong automotive industry, the Korean economy relies on the two largest customers for industrial robots.

**Singapore**follows with 770 robots per 10,000 employees. Singapore is a small country with a very low number of employees in the manufacturing industry, so it can reach a high Robot density also with a relatively small operational stock.

**China** took third place in 2023, surpassing Germany and Japan. The country's push to the use of automation technology results in a high robot density of 470 robots per 10,000 employees (2022: 402 units). China only entered the top 10 in 2019. It has managed to double its robot density within four years.

**Germany**ranks fourth with 429 robots per 10,000 employees. The robot density of Europe´s largest economy has grown by 5% CAGR since 2018.

**Japan** is in fifth place with 419 units. Robot density of the world´s predominant robot manufacturing country grew by 7% on average each year (2018-2023).

Robot density in the **United States** reached 295 units in 2023. The country ranks tenth in the world.

About Robot density
-------------------

Robot density is the number of operational industrial robots relative to the number of employees. It can cover the whole manufacturing industry or just specific industrial branches. The number of employees serves as a measure of economic size, so the quotient of operational stock over employees puts the operational stock on a uniform base.

More than 10% of South Korea's workforce is now robotic, survey finds
=====================================================================

**By** Sarah Rumpf-Whitten

**Published**  November 23, 2024 9:07pm EST

[Technology](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/tag/technology)

[FOX Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/)

![Image 3](https://images.foxtv.com/static.livenowfox.com/www.livenowfox.com/content/uploads/2024/11/764/432/gettyimages-1733214249-scaled.jpg?ve=1&tl=1) article

FILE - An industrial robot arm assembling an EV battery pack on an automated production line. Getty Images

Slightly over 10% of South Korea's workforce has been replaced [with robots](https://www.foxbusiness.com/technology), an annual survey by World Robotics 2024 found.

[The report](https://ifr.org/ifr-press-releases/news/global-robot-density-in-factories-doubled-in-seven-years), which was presented by the International Federation of Robotics (IFR), found that robotics has continued on an upward trend globally.

South Korea led the transition to a robotic workforce, with the Asian country having 1,012 robots per 10,000 employees.

The country has increased its use of robots by 5% each year since 2018, the IFR found.

[**FORMER FACEBOOK EXEC SAYS AI ROBOTS WILL SOON COMPLETE HOUSEHOLD CHORES AMID HUMAN REPLACEMENT CONCERN**](https://www.foxbusiness.com/media/former-facebook-exec-ai-robots-soon-complete-household-chores-human-replacement-concerns)

**How does the U.S. compare?**
------------------------------

[Singapore](https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/major-airline-spend-over-800m-upgrade-cabins-long-haul-aircraft) came in second with 770 robots per 10,000 employees, the organization found.

China, with 470 robots per 10,000 employees, has overtaken Germany and Japan, and landed in third place behind Singapore.

[**ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IS BIG, BUT ARE COMPANIES HIRING FOR AI ROLES TOO FAST?**](https://www.foxbusiness.com/technology/artificial-intelligence-big-companies-hiring-ai-roles-too-fast)

[Germany](https://www.foxbusiness.com/category/fox-news-german) came in fourth place with 429 robots per 10,000 employees, followed by Japan with 419 units per 10,000 employees.

The United States ranked 10th with 295 robots per 10,000 employees.

**Robot density by region**
---------------------------

The IFR found that the [European Union](https://www.foxbusiness.com/category/europe) has a robot density of 219 units per 10,000 employees, an increase of 5.2% from previous years.

Germany, Sweden, Denmark and Slovenia led the increase in robotic adoption, with the countries landing in the global top ten.

North America's robot density is 197 units per 10,000 employees – up 4.2%, the IFR found.

Asia has a robot density of 182 units per 10,000 persons employed in manufacturing - an increase of 7.6%, the IFR found.

Korea, Singapore, China and Japan were ranked in the top ten most automated countries.

Fox News has reached out to the International Federation of Robotics for comment.

88.title: 亚洲（中日韩）、欧洲（德国）和美国的机器人研发计划概况
88.description: 王德生|机器人,密度,研发|国际机器人联合会（IFR）2025年2月11日在德国法兰克福发布的《2025年世界机器人研发计划》（WorldRoboticsRDPrograms2025）显示，全球各大经济体正在投资机器人技术，以支持工业和社会发展。然而，各国政府对机器人研发（RD）计划采取了不同的策略。一、中国中国的《“十四五”机器人产业发展规划》将持续至2025年。该计划由工业和信息化部（MIIT）于2021年12月在北京发
88.content:
国际机器人联合会（IFR）2025 年 2 月 11 日 在德国法兰克福发布的《2025 年世界机器人研发计划》（World Robotics R&D Programs 2025）显示，全球各大经济体正在投资机器人技术，以支持工业和社会发展。然而，各国政府对机器人研发（R&D）计划采取了不同的策略。

**一、****中国**

中国的《“十四五”机器人产业发展规划》将持续至 2025 年。该计划由工业和信息化部（MIIT）于 2021 年 12 月在北京发布，重点推动创新，旨在使中国成为全球机器人技术和工业发展的领导者。“智能机器人重点专项”于 2024 年 7 月更新，预算约为 4520 万美元（约合 3.29 亿人民币），促进国家经济关键独立领域的发展。核心目标包括基础前沿技术，例如生成式人工智能（AI）模型的训练。

据 IFR 2024 年 11 月 20 日 发布的世界机器人最新 数据，中国积极推动自动化技术的应用，中国制造业的机器人密度在 2023 年达到每万名 员工配有 470 台 机器人（2022 年为 402 台），全球排名第三（见下 图）。中国直至 2019 年才跻身前十，但在短短四年内将其机器人密度翻倍。

![Image 1: The graph shows the number of robots per 10,000 employees in various countries](blob:http://localhost/b4bcfcdb1e6e5d742a2204fb81d88039)

**图 2023 年全球制造业机器人密度情况（按国家/地区排名）（单位：台）**

资料来源：IFR.Global Robot Density in Factories Doubled in Seven Years.2024-11-20.

**二、****日本**

日本的“新机器人战略”旨在使该国成为全球机器人创新中心。重点行业包括制造业、护理与医疗以及农业，核心方向保持不变。2020 年启动的“登月研发计划”（Moonshot Research and Development Program）将持续至 2050 年，预算达 4.4 亿美元（250 亿日元）。该计划设定十大目标，涵盖社会、环境和经济领域，以实现“人类福祉”，解决人口老龄化和全球变暖等未来社会问题。此外，该计划促进 AI 机器人自主学习、环境适应、智能进化，并与人类协作。

据 IFR 2024 年 11 月 20 日 发布的世界机器人最新 数据，日本是全球最大的工业机器人制造国。机器人密度 全球排名第五，每万名 员工配有 419 台 机器人。

**三、****韩国**

韩国政府于 2024 年 1 月公布《第四次智能机器人基本计划》，该计划将持续至 2028 年。政府投资 1.28 亿美元（1800 亿韩元）支持机器人产业发展，使其成为第四次工业革命的核心产业，并推动制造业和服务业的创新。核心目标包括提升技术水平、培养专业人才、增强企业竞争力，以巩固韩国机器人产业的基础。此外，该国计划加强企业间、国际间和地区间的战略合作，以促进机器人产业的发展。

据 IFR 的世界机器人 最新数据，韩国是全球工业机器人采用率最高的国家，机器人密度达到每万名员工 1012 台。自 2018 年以来，韩国的机器人密度平均每年增长 5%。

**四、****欧洲**

“地平线欧洲”（Horizon Europe）是欧盟的关键研究与创新框架计划，预算为 1000 亿美元（955 亿欧元），将持续至 2027 年。其主要目标包括：增强欧盟的科学与技术基础，提升欧洲的创新能力和竞争力。2023-2025 年机器人相关工作计划的总资金达 1.835 亿美元（1.74 亿欧元），部分内容于 2024 年 4 月更新，重点关注 AI、数据与机器人、清洁能源转型、创新医疗等领域。

据 IFR 的 世界机器人 最新数据，欧盟的机器人密度为每万名 员工 219 台，其中德国、瑞典、丹麦和斯洛文尼亚跻身全球前十。

**五、****德国**

德国的研发与创新计划“高科技战略 2025”（HTS）将持续至 2026 年，总预算达 3.692 亿美元（3.5 亿欧元）。“机器人研究行动计划”旨在促进研究中心的互联互通，构建“德国机器人研究所”（Robotics Institute Germany），支持专业人才培养，并将机器人研究成果应用于实际。

据 IFR 的 世界机器人 最新数据，德国是欧洲最大的机器人市场，其机器人密度全球排名第四，为每万名员工 429 台。

**六、****美国**

美国的机器人研发计划涵盖多个领域，包括国家科学基金会（NSF）主导的智能机器人与自主系统基础研究、美国国家航空航天局（NASA）推进的“太空机器人”计划，以及国防部（DoD）管理的“军事机器人与自主车辆”项目。继火星探测计划之后，NASA 启动“阿尔忒弥斯计划”（Artemis），旨在 2024 年后将宇航员送往月球表面，并为未来火星任务开发相关能力。该计划在 2021-2025 财年的总预算为 530 亿美元。

NSF 的研究项目支持机器人技术在工作场所、医院、社区和家庭中的应用，2024 年预算约为 7000 万美元。DoD 的 2023 年预算中，自动化与机器人技术投资达到 103 亿美元。

IFR 的 世界机器人 最新数据 显示，美国 2024 年的机器人密度达到每万名员工 295 台，全球排名第十。在工业机器人年度安装量方面，美国位居全球第三。

**主要参考资料：**

1、IFR.Robotics Research: How Asia, Europe and America Invest.2025-02-11.

[https://ifr.org/ifr-press-releases/news/robotics-research-goverment-programs-asia-europe-and-america-2025](https://www.istis.sh.cn/cmsnull "登录后可点击跳转")

2、IFR.Global Robot Density in Factories Doubled in Seven Years.2024-11-20.

Market Intelligence

 Equipment and Machinery  South Korea  Trade Development  Government Influence Issues 

South Korea Robotics Industry
=============================

The Korean robotics industry experienced significant growth in recent years, driven by machine learning, advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), and sensor technologies. Korea has the world’s highest robot density with 1,012 installed robots per 10,000 manufacturing workers which is more than six times the global average, [according to the International Federation of Robotics (IFR)](https://www.robotics247.com/article/ifr_report_world_robotics_rd_programs_sees_how_asia_europe_u_s_invest "(opens in a new window)"). Korea seeks an accelerated convergence of robots and AI across industries to address shrinking working-age populations, to reduce hazardous labor environments, and to increase product efficiency.

Korea is at the forefront of robotics innovation, with its government investing heavily in research and development to drive technological advancements. In January 2024, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) announced the Fourth Intelligent Robot Basic Plan (2024-2028) aiming to invest over US$2.24 billion in the public and private sectors by 2030. This initiative outlines the development direction for the robot industry across key industries, ranging from manufacturing to services, agriculture, logistics, healthcare, defense, and social safety. It includes the goal to establish an efficient system for securing technology to raise the local manufacturing rate of core robot parts from the current 44 percent to 80 percent by 2030 and improve or eliminate 51 regulatory obstacles. In accordance with the Promotion of Development and Deployment of Intelligence Robots Act, the MOTIE will update the basic plan every five years to ensure the continuous advancement of the robot industry.

U.S. companies can find market opportunities in Korea as the robotics market is poised for substantial growth, driven by the increasing adoption in a wide array of robotic applications, including industrial robots, service robots, medical robots, and autonomous vehicles. Manufacturing robots account for 50 percent of the Korean robot market, leading the market growth. The share of service robots stands at 16 percent, but it has entered an explosive growth stage. Korea imports a large share of high-tech industrial robot components from overseas. With government plans, Korea will concentrate on eight core technologies: servomotors, controllers, reducers, sensors, grippers, autonomous movement software, autonomous operation software and human-robot interaction systems for various robot applications.

U.S. suppliers in this sector should sign up for the upcoming Supply Chain Commercial Dialogue Robotics Industry Showcase webinar in December 2024! Registration will open in November 2024.

For more information contact the U.S. Commercial Service in South Korea:

Jessica Son, Senior Commercial Specialist, Email: [jessica.son@trade.gov](mailto:jessica.son@trade.gov)

Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta
--------------------------------------

Welcome to the Global Business Navigator, an artificial intelligence (AI) Chatbot from the International Trade Administration (ITA). This tool, currently in beta version testing, is designed to provide general information on the exporting process and the resources available to assist new and experienced U.S. exporters. The Chatbot, developed using Microsoft’s Azure AI services, is trained on ITA’s export-related content and aims to quickly get users the information they need. The Chatbot is intended to make the benefits of exporting more accessible by understanding non-expert language, idiomatic expressions, and foreign languages.

### Limitations

As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the [Export Solutions](https://www.trade.gov/export-solutions) web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. Always double-check the Chatbot’s responses using the provided references or by visiting the [Export Solutions](https://www.trade.gov/export-solutions) web pages on Trade.gov. Do not use its responses as legal or professional advice. Inaccurate advice from the Chatbot would not be a defense to violating any export rules or regulations.

### Privacy

The Chatbot does not collect information about users and does not use the contents of users’ chat history to learn new information. All feedback is anonymous. Please do not enter personally identifiable information (PII), sensitive, or proprietary information into the Chatbot. Your conversations will not be connected to other interactions or accounts with ITA. Conversations with the Chatbot may be reviewed to help ITA improve the tool and address harmful, illegal, or otherwise inappropriate questions.

### Translation

The Chatbot supports a wide range of languages. Because the Chatbot is trained in English and responses are translated, you should verify the translation. For example, the Chatbot may have difficulty with acronyms, abbreviations, and nuances in a language other than English.

76.content:
世界各国投资机器人技术以支持工业和社会的发展。国际机器人联合会（IFR）发表《世界机器人研发计划》，研究了当今亚洲、欧洲和美国政府正式推动的机器人研究资助计划（R&D）。报告显示，就每年安装的工业机器人而言，最先进的机器人技术国家和地区（包括中国、日本、美国、韩国、德国和欧盟）推动了截然不同的研发战略。

**一、中国**

中国工业和信息化部（MIIT）于2021年12月21日发布《“十四五”机器人产业发展规划》，该规划的重点是促进创新，目标是使中国成为机器人技术和产业进步的全球领导者。机器人被列入未来五年的8个重点行业之一。为贯彻落实国家科技创新部署，国家重点研发计划重点专项“智能机器人”于2022年4月23日启动，投入资金4350万美元。IFR最近公布的统计年鉴《世界机器人》显示，2021年，中国制造业的机器人密度达到每万名工人322台，全球排名第五，而2018年排名第20位（140台）。

**二、日本**

日本实施的《机器人新战略》旨在使日本成为全球第一的机器人技术创新高地。2022年，日本政府提供了9.305亿美元的资金，重点支持领域包括：制造业（7780万美元）、照护与医疗（5500万美元）、基础设施（6.432亿美元）和农业（6620万美元）。在制造业和服务业的行动方案中列出的项目包括自动化驾驶、先进的空中移动技术，以及下一代人工智能和机器人的核心集成技术等。在2020年至2025年的《登月（Moonshot）研发计划》中，机器人相关的项目获得了日本政府4.4亿美元的支持。根据IFR《全球机器人报告》的数据显示，日本是全世界排名第一的工业机器人制造国，2021年生产的机器人数量占全球总量的45%。

**三、韩国**

韩国政府出台的《第三版智[](https://www.cmes.org/library/recom/3cf77590c9ba4537a4a72f34fc071219.html)能机器人发展计划》，旨在推动韩国在第四次工业革命中大力发展机器人，使其成为核心产业。韩国政府为《2022智能机器人行动计划》投资1.722亿美元，并将在2022至2024年为《专用载人或无人机全尺寸试验平台项目》投资741万美元。根据IFR《全球机器人报告》的数据显示，韩国2021年的工业机器人密度达到创纪录的1000台，标志着韩国成为全世界机器人密度最高的国家。

**四、欧盟**

《欧洲地平线》是欧盟的重点科研创新框架计划，2021-2027年的资助金额达943亿美元。其关键目标包括增强欧盟的科研基础，强化欧洲的创新能力、竞争力和就业率以及注重民生重点和和可持续社会经济的发展模式和价值。欧洲委员会在2021-2022年间为机器人相关的项目提供了1.985亿美元的资金支持。

**五、德国**

《2025高科技战略（HTS）》是德国政府出台的第四版研发创新计划。德国政府每年都将提供6900万美元的资金，截止到2026年总投资额达3.45亿美元。同时，作为HTS2025任务的一部分，推出了“为人民塑造技术”计划。该计划旨在利用整个社会和产业的技术变革，造福于人民。研究主题包括：数字辅助系统（如数据眼镜、人机协作、助力体力工作工的外骨骼），以及工作流程的柔性解决方案和支持移动操作的解决方案。根据IFR《全球机器人报告》的数据显示，德国是欧洲最大的机器人市场，机器人密度全球位居第四，每万名工人有397台机器人。

**六、美国**

美国发布的《国家机器人计划（NRI）》是政府支持的机器人基础研发方案。2021年2月，美国推出了NIR3.0，在原来的NRI基础上重点关注机器人集成系统的研发。2021年，美国政府为NRI3.0投资了1400万美元，鼓励学术、产业、政府、非盈利组织和其他组织之间开展合作。美国航空航天局（NASA）推出的“从月球到火星”计划强调在月球附近和月球上建立长期驻留设施。这些科技发展项目的目标是显著提高机器人的性能，配合人类进行深空探索和科学任务。美国政府还计划在2020年至2024年期间，对阿尔忒弥斯（Artemis）登月计划提供350亿美元的资助。根据IFR《全球机器人报告》的数据显示，2021年，美国的机器人密度从2020年的255台增加到274台，全球排名第九。同年，美国的工业机器人年度安装量位列全世界第三名。

85.title: Robotik-Forschung: So investieren Asien, Europa und Amerika
85.description: Während Asien Milliarden in die Robotik-Branche investierte, ziehen Europa und die USA mit ambitionierten Strategien nach. Wer führt das Rennen an?
85.content:
Anzeige

World Robotics R&D Programs

Während Asien Milliarden in die Robotik-Branche investierte, ziehen Europa und die USA mit ambitionierten Strategien nach. Wer führt das Rennen an – und welche Technologien stehen im Mittelpunkt? Ein Blick auf die globalen Trends und Investitionen.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Die staatlichen Forschungs- und Entwicklungsprogramme (F&E) weltweit verfolgen unterschiedliche Strategien: Die International Federation of Robotics analysiert mit dem Report 'World Robotics R&D Programs 2025' offizielle Förderprogramme in Asien, Europa und Amerika.

(Bild: Naturalis - stock.adobe.com)

Anzeige

Volkswirtschaften in aller Welt investieren in Robotik, um Industrie und Gesellschaft zu unterstützen. Die staatlichen Forschungs- und Entwicklungsprogramme (F&E) verfolgen allerdings ganz unterschiedliche Strategien: Die International Federation of Robotics analysiert mit dem Report ‚World Robotics R&D Programs 2025‘ offizielle Förderprogramme in Asien, Europa und Amerika.

„Die vierte Auflage des Reports ‚World-Robotics-R&D-Programs‘ berichtet über die jüngsten Entwicklungen in den Förderprogrammen, inklusive der Aktualisierungen für 2024", sagt Prof. Dr. Jong-Oh Park, stellvertretender Vorsitzender des IFR-Forschungsausschusses und Mitglied des Executive Boards. „Wir haben insgesamt 13 Länder analysiert, wobei Singapur und Kanada zum ersten Mal in dieser Publikation ausführlich vorgestellt werden.“

Anzeige

Forschungs- und Entwicklungsprogramme im Überblick
--------------------------------------------------

In China läuft der '14th Five-Year Plan' für die Entwicklung der Roboterindustrie noch bis Ende 2025. Das Programm konzentriert sich auf die Förderung von Innovationen. Das Ministerium für Industrie und Informationstechnologie (MIIT) hatte den Startschuss im Dezember 2021 gegeben. Ziel ist es, China zu einer weltweit führenden Nation im Bereich der Robotertechnologie und der industriellen Entwicklung zu machen. Das 'Key Special Program on Intelligent Robots' wurde im Juli 2024 aktualisiert. Die Entwicklung unabhängiger Schlüsselsektoren für die Volkswirtschaft soll mit einem Budget von rund 45,2 Millionen USD (ca. 329 Millionen CNY) gefördert werden. Zu den Hauptzielen gehören grundlegende Spitzentechnologien, wie beispielsweise das Training generativer KI-Modelle.

Wie das jüngste statistische Jahrbuch 'World Robotics' der IFR zeigt, hat China in der verarbeitenden Industrie eine Roboterdichte von 470 Einheiten pro 10.000 Arbeiter erreicht: Damit liegt das Land im Jahr 2023 weltweit auf Platz 3. China ist erst 2019 in die Top-10-Liste aufgestiegen und hat es geschafft, seine Roboterdichte innerhalb von vier Jahren zu verdoppeln.

Anzeige

New Robot Strategy in Japan
---------------------------

In Japan zielt die 'New Robot Strategy' darauf ab, das Land zum weltweit führenden Zentrum für Roboterinnovationen zu machen. Zu den Schlüsselsektoren gehören unverändert das verarbeitende Gewerbe, Pflege und Medizin sowie die Landwirtschaft. Das 2020 ins Leben gerufene 'Moonshot Research and Development Program' wird bis 2050 laufen und mit einem Budget von 440 Millionen US-Dollar (25 Milliarden JPY) ausgestattet sein. Zehn definierte Moonshot-Ziele in den Bereichen Gesellschaft, Umwelt und Wirtschaft sollen das 'menschliche Wohlergehen' fördern. Dazu gehören beispielsweise Herausforderungen, mit denen das Land in Zukunft konfrontiert sein wird: Die Überalterung der Bevölkerung und die Erderwärmung. Das Programm fördert gezielt KI-Projekte, in denen Roboter autonom lernen, sich an ihre Umgebung anpassen, ihre künstliche Intelligenz weiterzuentwickeln und mit Menschen zusammenarbeiten.

Laut des statistischen IFR-Jahrbuches 'World Robotics' ist Japan der weltweit führende Hersteller von Industrierobotern. Bei der Roboterdichte rangiert das Land mit 419 Einheiten pro 10.000 Arbeitern weltweit auf dem fünften Platz.

Anzeige

Die Regierung in Südkoreakündigte im Januar 2024 den '4th Basic Plan on Intelligent Robots' mit einer Fördersumme von 128 Millionen USD (180 Milliarden KRW) und einer Laufzeit bis 2028 an. Der Plan zielt darauf ab, die Robotik als Kernindustrie der vierten industriellen Revolution zu entwickeln sowie Innovationen in der Fertigung und im Dienstleistungssektor zu fördern. Die koreanische Robotikindustrie soll mit verbesserter Technologie wettbewerbsfähiger werden. Darüber hinaus will das Land die strategische Kooperation von Unternehmen und die internationale und interregionale Zusammenarbeit in der Robotikindustrie stärken.

Korea: weltweiter Spitzenreiter beim Einsatz von Industrierobotern
------------------------------------------------------------------

Das statistische Jahrbuch ‚World Robotics‘ der IFR führt Korea mit 1.012 Robotern pro 10.000 Beschäftigte als weltweiten Spitzenreiter beim Einsatz von Industrierobotern auf. Die Roboterdichte hat sich seit 2018 jedes Jahr um durchschnittlich fünf Prozent erhöht.

‚Horizon Europe‘ ist mit einem Budget von 100 Milliarden US Dollar (95,5 Milliarden Euro) und einer Laufzeit bis 2027 das wichtigste Rahmenprogramm für Forschung und Innovation der EU. Die wichtigsten Ziele sind: Stärkung der wissenschaftlichen und technologischen Grundlagen der EU sowie Förderung der Innovationskapazität und Wettbewerbsfähigkeit. Für das auf Robotik bezogene Arbeitsprogramm 2023 bis 2025 stellt die Europäische Kommission insgesamt 183,5 Millionen US Dollar (174 Millionen Euro) bereit. Fokussiert wird auf eine industrielle Führungsposition in den Bereichen KI, Daten und Robotik, eine saubere Energiewende und innovative Gesundheitsinitiativen, um nur einige Beispiele zu nennen.

Anzeige

Deutschland ist größter Robotermarkt in Europa
----------------------------------------------

Die Europäische Union hat laut IFR-Statistik ‚World Robotics‘ eine Roboterdichte von 219 Einheiten pro 10.000 Beschäftigte. Deutschland, Schweden, Dänemark und Slowenien zählen dabei zu den Top-10 automatisierten Volkswirtschaften weltweit.

Die deutsche Hightech-Strategie 2025 (HTS) hat mit einem Gesamtbudget von 369,2 Millionen US Dollar (350 Millionen Euro) eine Laufzeit bis 2026. Der ‚Aktionsplan Robotikforschung‘ soll die Vernetzung von Forschungszentren als ‚Robotics Institute Germany‘ (RIG) unterstützen, Fachkräfte fördern und Robotik-Forschungsergebnisse in die Anwendung bringen. Deutschland ist laut ‚World Robotics‘ Statistik der größte Robotermarkt in Europa - die Roboterdichte liegt mit 429 Robotern pro 10.000 Beschäftigten weltweit an vierter Stelle.

Anzeige

Aktuelle Meldungen aus der Industrie
------------------------------------

Energiekrise, Lieferengpässe, Fachkräftemangel: Die Industrie steht vor vielen Herausforderungen. Alle Meldungen aus Maschinenbau und Co finden Sie in unserem News-Blog. [Hier klicken!](https://www.produktion.de/wirtschaft/deutz-verdient-im-dritten-quartal-deutlich-mehr-286669-900.html)

Viel Grundlagenforschung zu intelligenten Robotern in den USA
-------------------------------------------------------------

In den USA gehören zu den öffentlichen Förderprogrammen im Bereich Robotik in erster Linie die Grundlagenforschung zu intelligenten Robotern und autonomen Systemen der National Science Foundation (NSF), die Weltraumrobotik der NASA und das Programm ‚Military Robotics and Autonomous Vehicles‘ des Verteidigungsministeriums (DoD). Nach dem Mars-Erkundungsprogramm startete die NASA im Mai 2019 das Projekt Artemis, um Astronauten auf die Mondoberfläche zu schicken und neue Fähigkeiten für Marsmissionen nach 2024 zu entwickeln. Das Gesamtbudget für Artemis beträgt für die Haushaltsjahre 2021 bis 2025 insgesamt 53 Milliarden US Dollar.

Die NSF-Forschungsprogramme unterstützen Entwicklung und Einsatz von Robotern am Arbeitsplatz, in Krankenhäusern, in Gemeinden und in Haushalten. Das für 2024 beantragte Budget beläuft sich auf rund 70 Millionen US Dollar. Der Haushalt 2023 des US-Verteidigungsministeriums beinhaltete für Robotik und autonome Technologien insgesamt 10,3 Milliarden US Dollar.

Anzeige

Im internationalen Vergleich rangieren die USA laut IFR-Statistik ‚World Robotics‘ mit einer Roboterdichte von 295 Einheiten pro 10.000 Beschäftigte weltweit auf Rang 10. Bei den jährlichen Installationen von Industrierobotern liegen die USA weltweit auf dem 3. Platz.

86.title: Robotics Research: How Asia, Europe and America Invest – Global Report 2023 by IFR
86.description: Countries around the world invest in robotics to support developments in industry and society. What are the exact targets of robotics research funding programs (R&D) officially driven by governments in Asia, Europe and America today? This has been researched by the International Federation of Robotics and published in the 2023 update paper of “World Robotics R&D Programs”.
86.content:
Countries around the world invest in robotics to support developments in industry and society. What are the exact targets of robotics research funding programs (R&D) officially driven by governments in Asia, Europe and America today? This has been researched by the International Federation of Robotics and published in the 2023 update paper of “World Robotics R&D Programs”.

![Image 1: The sun shines brightly over the Earth from space. A robotic arm is visible](https://ifr.org/downloads/press2018/space-Pixabay_1600x900.jpg)

“The 3rd version of World Robotics R&D Programs covers the latest funding developments including updates in 2022,” says Prof. Dr. Jong-Oh Park, Vice-Chairman IFR Research Committee and member of the Executive Board.

The overview shows that the most advanced robotics countries in terms of annual installations of industrial robots – China, Japan, USA, South Korea, Germany - and the EU drive very different R&D strategies:

Robotics R&D programs - officially driven by governments
--------------------------------------------------------

In **China**, the **“14 th Five-Year Plan” for Robot Industry Development**, released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) in Beijing on 21 st December 2021, focuses on promoting innovation. The goal is to make China a global leader for robot technology and industrial advancement. Robotics is included in 8 key industries for the next 5 years. In order to implement national science and technology innovation arrangements, the key special program “Intelligent Robots” was launched under the National Key R&D Plan on 23 rd April 2022 with a funding of 43.5 million USD. The recent statistical yearbook "World Robotics" by IFR shows that China reached a robot density of 322 units per 10,000 workers in the manufacturing industry: The country ranks 5 th worldwide in 2021 compared to 20 th (140 units) in 2018.

In **Japan**, the **“New Robot Strategy”** aims to make the country the world´s number one robot innovation hub. More than 930.5 million USD in support has been provided by the Japanese government in 2022. Key sectors are manufacturing (77.8 million USD), nursing and medical (55 million USD), infrastructure (643.2 million USD) and agriculture (66.2 million USD). The action plan for manufacturing and service includes projects such as autonomous driving, advanced air mobility or the development of integrated technologies that will be the core of next-generation artificial intelligence and robots. A budget of 440 million USD was allocated to robotics-related projects in the “Moonshot Research and Development Program” over a period of 5 years from 2020 to 2025. According to the statistical yearbook "World Robotics" by IFR, Japan is the world´s number one industrial robot manufacturer and delivered 45% of the global supply in 2021.

The **3rd Basic Plan on Intelligent Robots** of**South Korea** is pushing to develop robotics as a core industry in the fourth industrial revolution. The Korean government allocated 172.2 million USD in funding for the “2022 Implementation Plan for the Intelligent Robot”. From 2022 to 2024 a total of 7.41 million USD is planned in funding for the “Full-Scale Test Platform Project for Special-Purpose Manned or Unmanned Aerial Vehicles”. The statistical yearbook "World Robotics" showed an all-time high of 1,000 industrial robots per 10,000 employees in 2021. This makes Korea the country with the highest robot density worldwide.

**Horizon Europe** is the **European Union’s** key research and innovation framework program with a budget of 94.30 billion USD for seven years (2021-2027). Top targets are: strengthening the EU’s scientific and technological bases, boosting Europe’s innovation capacity, competitiveness and jobs as well as delivering on citizens’ priorities and sustaining socio-economic models and values. The European Commission provides total funding of 198.5 million USD for the robotics-related work program 2021-2022.

**Germany´s High-Tech Strategy 2025 (HTS)** is the fourth edition of the German R&D and innovation program. The German government will provide around 69 million USD annually until 2026 - a total budget of 345 million USD for five years. As part of the HTS 2025 mission, the program “Shaping technology for the people” was launched. This program aims to use technological change in society as a whole and in the world of work for the benefit of people. Research topics are: digital assistance systems such as data glasses, human-robot-collaboration, exoskeletons to support employees in their physical work, but also solutions for the more flexible organization of work processes or the support of mobile work. According to the report "World Robotics" by IFR, Germany is the largest robot market in Europe – the robot density ranks in 4 th place worldwide with 397 units per 10,000 employees.

The **National Robotics Initiative (NRI) i**n the **USA** was launched for fundamental robotics R&D supported by the US government. The **NRI-3.0 program**, announced in February 2021, seeks research on integrated robot systems and builds upon the previous NRI programs. The US government supported the NRI-3.0 fund to the sum of 14 million USD in 2021. Collaboration among academics, industry, government, non-profit, and other organizations is encouraged. The “Moon to Mars” project by NASA for example highlights objectives to establish a long-term presence in the vicinity of and on the moon. The projects target research and technology development that will significantly increase the performance of robots to collaboratively support deep space human exploration and science missions. For the Artemis lunar program, the US government is planning to allocate a budget of 35 billion USD from 2020 to 2024. The statistical yearbook "World Robotics" by IFR shows that robot density in the United States rose from 255 units in 2020 to 274 units in 2021. The country ranks 9th in the world. Regarding annual installations of industrial robots, the USA takes 3 rd position.

IFR Press contact
-----------------

Carsten Heer

E-Mail: press@ifr.org

Files for Download
------------------

Please find the information paper “World Robotics R&D Programs” by IFR for download at: [https://ifr.org/r-and-d](https://ifr.org/r-and-d) (download requires registration).

83.title: 数字图书馆
83.content:
2023 年 1 月 12 日，国际机器人联合会（IFR）研究并发布了《世界机器人研发计划》，该报告阐述了各国对机器人研发资助的最新进展，包括 2022 年的最新情况。报告指出，工业机器人的年度安装排名居前列的中国、日本、美国、韩国、德国和欧盟采用了截然不同的研发战略，具体如下：

●中国工信部（MIIT）于 2021 年 12 月 21 日在北京发布的机器人产业发展“十四五”规划的重点是促进创新，目标是使中国成为机器人技术和产业进步的全球领导者，机器人被列入未来 5 年的 8 个重点行业。为贯彻落实国家科技创新部署，2022 年 4 月 23 日，根据国家重点研发计划，启动了重点专项“智能机器人”，资金为 4350 万美元。IFR 最近发布的统计年鉴《世界机器人》显示，中国制造业机器人密度达到每万名工人 322 台：2021 年中国在全球排名第 5 位，而 2018 年排名第 20 位（140 台）。

●日本的“新机器人战略”旨在使该国成为世界第一的机器人创新中心。日本政府在 2022 年提供了超过 9.305 亿美元的支持。重点领域是制造业（7780 万美元）、护理和医疗（5500 万美元）、基础设施（6.432 亿美元）和农业（6620 万美元）。制造业和服务业行动计划包括自动驾驶、先进空中机动性或将成为下一代人工智能和机器人核心的集成技术开发等项目。从 2020 年到 2025 年的 5 年期间，“登月研究与发展计划”中机器人相关项目的预算为 4.4 亿美元。根据 IFR 的统计年鉴《世界机器人》，日本是世界第一大工业机器人制造商，2021 年其工业机器人供应量占全球的 45%。

●韩国第三次智能机器人基本计划正在推动将机器人技术发展为第四次工业革命的核心产业。韩国政府为“智能机器人 2022 年实施计划”拨款 1.722 亿美元。2022 年至 2024 年，“特种有人或无人飞行器全尺寸试验平台项目”计划资助 741 万美元。IFR 的统计年鉴《世界机器人》显示，2021 年，韩国每万名员工拥有 1 千台工业机器人，创历史新高，这使韩国成为全球机器人密度最高的国家。

●“欧洲地平线（Horizon Europe）”是欧盟的重点研究和创新框架计划，预算为 943 亿美元，为期七年（2021 年至 2027 年）。首要目标是：加强欧盟的科技基础，提升欧洲的创新能力、竞争力和就业机会，以及实现公民的优先事项并维持社会经济模式和价值观。欧盟委员会为 2021-2022 年机器人相关工作计划提供了总计 1.985 亿美元的资金。

●德国的 2025 高科技战略（HTS）是德国研发和创新计划的第四版。到 2026 年，德国政府每年将提供约 6900 万美元的资金——五年的总预算为 3.45 亿美元。作为 HTS 2025 使命的一部分，启动了“为人民塑造技术”计划。该计划旨在利用整个社会和工作领域的技术变革造福于人们。研究课题包括：数字辅助系统，例如数据眼镜、人机协作、支持员工进行体力工作的外骨骼，以及更灵活地组织工作流程或支持移动工作的解决方案。根据 IFR 的《世界机器人》报告，德国是欧洲最大的机器人市场——机器人密度位居全球第四，每万名员工拥有 397 台机器人。

●美国国家机器人计划（NRI）是在美国政府的支持下发起的基础机器人研发。NRI-3.0 计划，于 2021 年 2 月宣布，寻求对集成机器人系统的研究，并以之前的 NRI 项目为基础。美国政府在 2021 年向 NRI-3.0 基金提供了 1400 万美元的支持。鼓励学术界、工业界、政府、非营利组织和其他组织之间的合作。例如，美国国家航空航天局的“月球到火星”项目强调了在月球附近和月球上建立长期存在的目标。这些项目的目标研究和技术开发将显着提高机器人的性能，以协同支持深空人类探索和科学任务。对于阿尔忒弥斯登月计划，美国政府计划从 2020 年到 2024 年拨出 350 亿美元的预算。根据 IFR 的《世界机器人》报告，，美国的机器人密度从 2020 年的 255 台增加到 2021 的 274 台，全球排名第 9。关于工业机器人的年度安装，美国位居第三。

国际机器人联合会发布《2025年世界机器人报告》
========================

2025-10-14 17:30·[报告研究所](http://m.toutiao.com/c/user/token/MS4wLjABAAAAfiSN0ZzUCDXwHjzVeTfmnhxBViWYv5CPzHwlGSZq-j4/?source=tuwen_detail)

国际机器人联合会最新发布的《2025年世界机器人报告》统计数据显示，2024年全球工业机器人销量达54.2万台，较十年前增长超过两倍。年度销量连续第四年突破50万台。2024年亚洲地区占全球销量的74%，欧洲占16%，美洲占9%。

![Image 2: The graph displays the annual installations of industrial robots worldwide, measured in 1,000 units. The data spans from 2014 to 2024, with installations increasing from 221 in 2014 to 542 in 2024](https://p3-sign.toutiaoimg.com/tos-cn-i-axegupay5k/a889af57e57744248fc92df582ac9c3b~tplv-tt-origin-web:gif.jpeg?_iz=58558&from=article.pc_detail&lk3s=953192f4&x-expires=1766990872&x-signature=EYN4cRN8qYoLw449mzL202Jd0c4%3D)

2014年至2024年全球工业机器人年销量

国际机器人联合会主席伊藤隆之表示：“2024年工业机器人年销量位居历史第二高位，仅比两年前创下的历史峰值低2%。随着众多产业加速向数字化与自动化时代转型，工业机器人需求呈现爆发式增长。2024年全球工业机器人在役总量达466.4万台，同比增长9%。”

**亚洲、欧洲与美洲市场概览**

中国以54%遥遥领先的占比稳居2024年全球最大市场，最新数据显示销量达29.5万台，创年度新高。中国本土厂商首次在本国市场实现对外资品牌的超越，国内市场占有率从十年前的28%跃升至57%。2024年中国工业机器人在役总量突破200万台，居全球首位。而机器人行业在中国持续开拓新市场，机器人的市场需求仍会保持增长态势。2028年之前，中国制造业仍存在巨大潜力，可实现年均10%的增长。

日本以4.45万台销量维持全球第二大市场地位，同比略降4%。在役存量增长3%至45.05万台。2025年需求将恢复低个位数增长，未来数年增速将提升至中个位数水平。

韩国2024年的销量为3.06万台，同比下降3%，自2019年以来，韩国年销量维持3.1万台左右水平，成为继美国、日本、中国之后的全球第四大机器人市场。

印度以9,100台销量创历史新高，同比增长7%。其中汽车制造业以45%的市场份额成为主要驱动力，印度在全球销量排名中位列第六，较往年上升一位，紧随德国。

**欧洲**

欧洲工业机器人销量2024年下降8%至8.5万台，仍为历史次高纪录。欧盟占比80%（6.78万台），近岸外包趋势持续推动需求。2019-2024年均复合增长率达3%。

德国以26,982台销量位居欧洲最大市场及全球第五大市场，同比下降5%。这是继2023年创纪录年份后的第二高年度表现，占欧洲年度总销量的32%。意大利以8,783台同比下降16%，位居欧洲第二，西班牙（5,100台）凭借汽车产业强劲需求位居欧洲第三，法国（4,900台）同比下滑24%，位列第四。

英国2024年工业机器人销量同比下降35%至2,500台。2023年创纪录的3,800台为一次性峰值，主要受"超级折旧扣除"税收优惠政策刺激，该政策自2023年第一季度结束后需求即回落。过去十年呈现周期性波动，2024年全球排名下滑至第19位。

**美洲**

美洲地区连续四年销量突破5万台，2024年达50,100台，同比2023年下降10%。

美国作为美洲最大的区域市场，在2024年占美洲销量的68%。机器人销量同比下降9%至34,200台。美国主要从日本和欧洲进口机器人，本土供应商较少。然而，美国拥有众多本土机器人系统集成商，致力于提供机器人自动化解决方案。

墨西哥2024年销量5,600台，同比下降4%，其中汽车产业以63%的装机量占比保持主导地位。

加拿大销量为3,800台，同比下降12%。加拿大销量很大程度上取决于汽车投资周期。汽车业在2024年安装量占比为47%。

**行业展望**

经合组织（OECD）与国际货币基金组织（IMF）预测，2025年全球经济增长将在2.9%至3.0%区间，2026年将在2.9%至3.1%区间。然而，地缘政治紧张局势、东欧与中东地区的暴力冲突以及贸易干扰，正对全球经济产生负面影响。

机器人行业虽无法避免全球宏观经济环境影响，但预计整体仍将保持长期增长的趋势。尽管区域趋势差异显著，全球整体发展轨迹仍保持积极态势。预计2025年全球机器人销量将增长6%至57.5万台，2028年将突破70万台大关。

The Rise of AI Robotics in China
--------------------------------

### UnTree Robotics and the Kung Fu Robot

China's UnTree Robotics, a frontrunner in the field, has recently unveiled a humanoid robot capable of complex maneuvers, resembling a 'kung fu giant'. This showcases a significant leap in AI-driven motor skills and adaptability.

### Comparing China and the US in AI Robotics

The US, while having historically been a leader in robotics through companies like Boston Dynamics, is now facing increased competition from China.

![Image 65: News panel with a man in a suit on the left, a graphic video in the middle showing a white robot walking next to a robotic dog, and a Royal Care advertisement on the right](https://cdn.louhu.com/5iujaw01000dcjo950pnwykx72sj68jp.jpeg)
The Boston Dynamics' robots have long been renowned for their impressive agility and dexterity, however, the Chinese robots are rapidly closing the gap, while some argue, that they have already surpassed the performance levels.

**Several factors contribute to China's rapid progress:**

*   **Focus on Practical Applications:** China emphasizes deploying AI and robotics in real-world scenarios, such as manufacturing and logistics, which generates valuable data and drives further innovation.
*   **Access to Data:** China's large population and less stringent data privacy regulations provide its AI developers with access to vast amounts of data, crucial for training and improving AI algorithms.
*   **Strong Manufacturing Base:** China's established manufacturing infrastructure facilitates the rapid prototyping and production of robots, enabling quick iterations and cost-effective scaling.

### The Ethical and Societal Concerns

China's AI robotics revolution raises several ethical and societal questions.

![Image 66: A news program is being broadcast showing robot dogs being walked on leashes and an advertisement promoting collagen peptides](https://cdn.louhu.com/5iujaw01000dcjo9530rvoox73xdfwsh.jpeg)
The increasing reliance on AI in decision-making processes raises concerns about bias, transparency, and accountability. It is essential to ensure that AI systems are developed and deployed ethically, with safeguards in place to prevent discrimination and protect individual rights. **Concerns include:**

*   **Bias in Algorithms:** AI algorithms can perpetuate and amplify existing biases present in the data they are trained on, leading to discriminatory outcomes.
*   **Lack of Transparency:** The 'black box' nature of some AI systems makes it difficult to understand how decisions are being made, hindering accountability.
*   **Job Displacement:** The automation of tasks previously performed by humans raises concerns about job displacement and the need for workforce retraining programs.

To mitigate these risks, China needs to prioritize ethical AI development and promote transparency and accountability in AI systems. This includes establishing clear guidelines for AI development, implementing robust auditing mechanisms, and investing in education and training programs to prepare the workforce for the future of work.

### The Question of US Response

The US needs to take a comprehensive approach to address the challenges posed by China's AI robotics revolution. This includes investing in its own AI research and development, fostering a more supportive ecosystem for robotics companies, and addressing the ethical and societal implications of AI. **Specifically, the US should:**

*   **Increase Government Funding:** Increase funding for AI research and development, with a focus on both basic research and practical applications.
*   **Streamline Regulations:** Streamline regulations to facilitate the development and deployment of AI technologies, while ensuring ethical considerations are addressed.
*   **Promote Public-Private Partnerships:** Foster collaboration between government, industry, and academia to accelerate innovation and talent development in AI robotics.
*   **Invest in Education and Training:** Invest in education and training programs to prepare the workforce for the jobs of the future, focusing on skills that complement AI and automation.

The US also needs to carefully consider its approach to technology exports to China.

![Image 67: The news anchor stands in front of a large television screen, which is broadcasting a news segment on various topics](https://cdn.louhu.com/5iujaw01000dcjo957kox2wx743npzg1.jpeg)
While restrictions may be necessary to protect national security, they should be carefully targeted to avoid stifling innovation and hindering economic growth. A balanced approach that promotes both competition and collaboration is essential for maintaining US leadership in AI robotics.

The Future of Quantum Computing: How It Will Transform Technology by 2030
=========================================================================

[admin](https://milialar.org/author/admin/)[8 months ago](https://milialar.org/the-future-of-quantum-computing-how-it-will-transform-technology-by-2030/)[0](https://milialar.org/the-future-of-quantum-computing-how-it-will-transform-technology-by-2030/#comments)5 mins

![Image 13: The Future of Quantum Computing: How It Will Transform Technology by 2030](https://i1.wp.com/media.assettype.com/analyticsinsight/2025-02-21/0yqb2hqm/The-Next-Big-Leap-Predicting-Tech-Trends-for-2030.jpg?w=1200&h=675&auto=format%2Ccompress&fit=max&enlarge=true&resize=1200,666&ssl=1)

[**Quantum computing**](https://milialar.org/) is no longer just a theoretical concept—it’s rapidly becoming a reality. Companies like IBM, Google, and startups like Rigetti Computing are making breakthroughs that could redefine computing as we know it. By 2030, quantum computers may solve problems deemed impossible for classical computers, revolutionizing industries from medicine to cryptography.

In this article, we’ll explore:

*   What quantum computing is and how it differs from classical computing

*   Key breakthroughs in quantum technology

*   Real-world applications that will change industries

*   Challenges and ethical concerns

*   Predictions for quantum computing by 2030

**What Is Quantum Computing?**
------------------------------

Traditional computers use bits (0s and 1s) to process information. Quantum computers, however, use**quantum bits (qubits)**, which can exist in multiple states simultaneously thanks to**superposition**and**entanglement**.

### **Key Quantum Principles:**

1.   **Superposition**– A qubit can be 0, 1, or both at the same time.

2.   **Entanglement**– Linked qubits can instantly affect each other, even across distances.

3.   **Quantum Interference**– Enhances correct computation paths while canceling out errors.

This allows quantum computers to perform complex calculations exponentially faster than classical systems.

**Breakthroughs in Quantum Computing**
--------------------------------------

### **1. Quantum Supremacy Achieved (Google, 2019)**

Google’s Sycamore processor solved a problem in**200 seconds**that would take the world’s fastest supercomputer**10,000 years**.

### **2. Error Correction Improvements (IBM, 2023)**

IBM’s**133-qubit Heron processor**introduced better error correction, a major hurdle in quantum computing.

### **3. Modular Quantum Processors (Harvard-MIT, 2024)**

Researchers successfully linked multiple quantum chips, paving the way for scalable quantum systems.

**Real-World Applications of Quantum Computing**
------------------------------------------------

### **1. Drug Discovery & Healthcare**

Quantum computers can simulate molecular interactions at an atomic level, accelerating drug development. Example:

*   **COVID-19 drug research**could have been**10x faster**with quantum simulations.

### **2. Cryptography & Cybersecurity**

Quantum computers can break**RSA encryption**, forcing a shift to**quantum-resistant cryptography**.

### **3. Financial Modeling**

Banks like JPMorgan Chase are testing quantum algorithms for**risk assessment**and**fraud detection**.

### **4. Climate Science & Energy Optimization**

Quantum simulations could design**better batteries**and optimize**carbon capture**technologies.

**Challenges & Ethical Concerns**
---------------------------------

### **1. Technical Barriers**

*   **Qubit Stability**– Maintaining coherence is difficult due to environmental interference.

*   **Error Rates**– Quantum systems are prone to errors, requiring advanced correction methods.

### **2. Security Risks**

*   **Quantum hacking**threatens current encryption standards.

*   Governments are investing in**post-quantum cryptography**to prepare.

### **3. Accessibility & Cost**

*   Current quantum computers require**near-absolute-zero temperatures**, making them expensive.

*   Cloud-based quantum computing (e.g., IBM Quantum Experience) is helping democratize access.

**Predictions for Quantum Computing by 2030**
---------------------------------------------

1.   **Hybrid Systems**– Classical and quantum computers will work together for practical solutions.

2.   **Commercial Quantum Cloud Services**– AWS, Google, and Microsoft will offer quantum-as-a-service (QaaS).

3.   **First “Useful” Quantum Computer**– A machine that solves real-world business problems, not just lab experiments.

4.   **Regulatory Frameworks**– Governments will establish quantum computing policies for security and ethics.

**Conclusion**
--------------

Quantum computing is set to disrupt industries in ways we’re only beginning to understand. While challenges remain, the progress made in the last five years suggests that by 2030, quantum tech will be integral to scientific, financial, and cybersecurity advancements.
